answer: Beacon Terrace Pricing. Every identity must broadcast a periodic beacon; the protocol requires each beacon to cite a randomly assigned terrace of N prior identities, forcing provable mutual awareness. An attacker minting k identities must wire each into distinct terraces, and a gale of random audits replays citations, slashing any identity whose cited terrace members deny the link. Cost scales with k·N audit exposure, so fake identities pay real coordination overhead per node rather than a flat fee.
